e.etymology: Most often a respelling of Amy, from Old French Amee, beloved, which goes back to Latin amare, to love.
A modern American name built from Jay and Anna, in the same family as Jayla, Jaylynn and Jayda.

e.meaning: from a surname based on Alfred, elf counsel
e.etymology: A respelling of Avery, an English surname that grew out of the Norman French way of saying Alfred, Old English for elf counsel.
From O'Ryan, the Irish surname Ó Riain with its prefix kept; Ryan comes from the same surname. It sounds the same as Orion.
A modern American name built from Jay with the -line or -lene ending, a spelling of Jaylene.
In American use an elaboration of Bella, the short form of Isabella and Arabella. Abella is also a Catalan and Spanish surname from the word for bee.
e.note: Shared with Abella Danger, a widely known adult film performer.

e.etymology: From the surname Colden, taken from a place name in northern England. As a given name it sits beside Colton and Holden.
A name used mainly in Amish communities in the United States. Its shape follows Biblical names ending in -uel such as Samuel and Penuel.

e.meaning: dweller at the edge of town
e.etymology: An English surname from Middle English toun, village, and ende, end, for someone who lived at the outskirts of a village.
A respelling of Khloe and Chloe, from Greek khloe, a young green shoot, an epithet of the goddess Demeter.
e.note: The letter order invites the reading Cole and is often taken for a typo of Khloe.

e.etymology: A modern Caribbean Spanish coinage in the family of Ya- names such as Yadiel and Yadira. Catcher Yadier Molina made it familiar in the United States.

assoc.t: Yadier Molina, longtime St. Louis Cardinals catcher

e.etymology: A C- spelling of Kalina, a Slavic name from the word for the viburnum or guelder rose. Călina is a Romanian name from the same plant word.
A modern American name built from Ray and the -land ending of Ryland and Leland. It is close to Raylan, which spread after the TV series Justified began in 2010.
The Arabic name of a figure in the Quran who is usually identified with the Biblical Ezra, whose Hebrew name means help.
For boys a Yiddish short form of Eliyahu, the Hebrew name behind Elijah. For girls it is also a Russian pet form of names such as Elvira and Eleonora.
A form of Joshua that keeps the Y of the Hebrew original, Yehoshua, Yahweh is salvation.
A Yoruba sentence name: Oluwa, God or Lord, with dara, is good, and si mi, to me.
From Hebrew Ben-Tsiyon, a compound of ben, son, and Tsiyon, Zion. It is used mostly in Orthodox Jewish families.
Taken from the family name of Abdul Rahman Al-Sudais, imam of the Grand Mosque in Mecca, whose Quran recitation is heard around the Muslim world.
A modern American coinage in the family of Zaniyah and Aniyah, built on a Zen- opening with the -iyah ending.

e.meaning: pet form of Mildred, Millicent, Emilia and Camilla
e.etymology: A spelling of Millie, the pet form of Mildred, Millicent, Emilia, Amelia and Camilla. In Estonia Milli is a short form of Emilie.
e.note: The spelling matches the pop duo Milli Vanilli and the metric prefix milli-.

e.etymology: A respelling of Tinsley, an English surname from a place in South Yorkshire whose Old English name means Tynni's mound.

e.meaning: galaxy, a great system of stars
e.etymology: The English word, used as a name. It comes through Latin from Greek galaxias, milky, the Greek name for the Milky Way, from gala, milk.

assoc.t: galaxy, a system of stars such as the Milky Way

e.meaning: the Aras river; also eagle in Lithuanian
e.etymology: In Turkish, Azerbaijani and Persian use it is the name of the Aras, the river along the borders of Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan and Iran. In Lithuanian aras is a word for eagle.
The English word, used as a name. It came through Latin and Greek from ancient Egyptian.

assoc.t: oasis, a green place with water in a desert
Oasis, British rock band behind Wonderwall

e.etymology: A recent American coinage that joins the Ry- of Rylee and Ryan to the -elle ending of Brielle and Arielle.
A recent American coinage with the sound of Hayes, Hayden and Jason; it can also be read as a spelling of the surname Hazen.
A spelling of Rafe, the old English pronunciation of Ralph, which comes from Old Norse Rathulfr: counsel and wolf.
A recent American coinage that joins Maeve, the Irish name of a legendary queen, to the -ry ending of Avery and Emery.
A recent American coinage that puts a Ja- opening on Nova, the Latin word for new.
The Italian form of the Roman name Aelianus, a derivative of the family name Aelius. In the United States it also works as a longer form of Elian.
